free_tier.stated: Every new account gets €10 of credits on its personal team; every new team starts on Hobby, which is free, with no monthly fee and €20 of usage on paid Pro
free_tier.notes: Credits are prepaid and usage draws them down per second. Hobby runs five sandboxes and services at once with 16 GB of live memory and 10 GB of disk; sizes pico, micro, nano, small and medium are available, and always-on is not.

per_object_cap.stated: no object unit: the offer is a microVM; a recipe volume is 1 to 5 GB and a plain volume starts at 2 GB unless the spec sets gb

retention.stated: A briq goes to sleep after its sleep window unused, one hour by default; it keeps its disk and is not billed while asleep. Nothing is deleted because of time.

egress.terms: Disk and outbound traffic are not billed today. Egress is open except outbound mail: SMTP ports 25, 465 and 587 are forbidden by the abuse policy. A private TCP endpoint takes TLS 1.2 or later; inbound traffic reaches a briq only after it is published with expose.
egress.free_allowance: outbound traffic is not billed today

interface_detail: Remote MCP server at https://api.briq.cloud/mcp (Streamable HTTP, OAuth sign-in or API key), CLI installed with npm install -g @briq-cloud/cli, and REST API at https://api.briq.cloud/v1. MCP is not a term in the interface vocabulary.
tooling: The briq CLI, the REST API and the MCP server; an API key is a BRIQ_API_KEY bearer token, and clients connect from Claude, Cursor, VS Code, Codex, Gemini CLI or OpenCode.
chaining: A briq runs a sandbox, a database or any OCI image beside the agent, with a private stack network between them and a preview URL when a service is published, so an agent can apply migrations or run tests against real services and hand back results.

limits.value: Hobby: 5 sandboxes and services at once, 16 GB memory across live briqs, 10 GB disk held, sizes pico to medium, no always-on briqs
sleep after 1 hour unused by default, 5 minutes to 7 days configurable; a sleeping briq keeps its disk and is not billed

limits_note: A start, fork or wake needs available capacity; each credential's policy can set a lower concurrency limit, and dailySpendCapCents limits each agent per day. A call the plan does not allow fails with plan_limit (403).
binding_note: The Hobby plan's five concurrent briqs, 16 GB of live memory and 10 GB of disk are exhausted before the €10 credit runs out at the published per-hour rates, and sleeping keeps the disk but does not free the plan allowance for a sixth live briq.

identity_cost.detail: The sign-up page offers Continue with Google, Continue with GitHub, or Name, Email and Password with at least 8 characters; the terms grant the €10 credit once the email address is confirmed. No card is required for Hobby or the credit, though pay-as-you-go past the credit needs a card on file.

reliability_note: A briq stops at zero balance without a card and nothing wakes until a top-up; an agent's daily spend cap stops its briqs when crossed; outbound SMTP is forbidden; a sleeping briq keeps its disk and nothing is deleted because of time.
confidence_note: The per-second euro rates, €10 credit, plan table and egress terms are quoted from the vendor's own cost, security and sign-up pages read on 2026-11-24; the sleep behaviour is from the vendor's lifecycle page on the same day.
